title: Grateful Dead Live at Hollywood Bowl on 1967-09-15
lineage: AUD > MC > R > R > NR > DAT > CDR > EAC (secure) > Cool Edit (remove isolated pops) > mkwACT > SHN (seekable)

ai_review.summary: Crude audience recording captures a high‑energy 1967 Hollywood Bowl set with Jerry’s soaring guitar, Pigpen’s organ/harmonica duels and standout jams like Viola Lee Blues despite frequent drop‑outs.
ai_review.review: The show is praised for its vibrant 1967 vibe – Jerry Garcia’s lead work, Pigpen’s organ and harmonica exchanges, and solid rhythm from Phil Lesh keep the momentum rolling through jams such as Viola Lee Blues, Alligator and Morning Dew. The audience (AUD) source suffers from hiss, drop‑outs and a generally muffled mix, but fans accept it as typical of the era and appreciate the historic ambience.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the performance highly (4‑5 stars) while consistently noting poor to fair audio quality; weighting show (70%) and recording (30%) yields an overall ~4‑star rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Frequent drop‑outs, hiss and muffled mids; crowd noise is prominent but adds period ambience. Mix is crude by modern standards but typical for 1966‑68 audience tapes.

standout_songs: Beat It On Down The Line
show_quality.setlist_flow: Starts with short, snappy numbers before launching into extended psychedelic jams; the energy builds as the band feeds off the crowd, ending on a high‑octane improvisational stretch.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for his soaring lead guitar and tight control during Morning Dew and other jams.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for thumping fretless bass that underpins the groove; described as solid throughout.
